title: Sanger Institute joins $1.8 billion international AI biology collaboration
source_used: Newswise (Biohub, DOE and NIH release of 7 Oct 2026)
key_facts: On 7 Oct 2026 Biohub, the US Department of Energy, the National Institutes of Health and new funding partners announced a $1.8 billion Virtual Biology Initiative to generate open, AI-ready biological data.
DOE will invest more than $500 million over five years; NIH will coordinate datasets from more than $500 million in earlier federal investment.
Google DeepMind, Isomorphic Labs and Meta are collectively investing $300 million.
Biohub's founding commitment is $500 million ($400 million for new measurement technologies, $100 million for outside research).

Leading institutions named as helping organise the scientific community include the Allen Institute, Broad Institute, Gladstone Institutes, the Human Cell Atlas, the Human Protein Atlas and the Wellcome Sanger Institute.
NVIDIA supports the initiative with computing; Renaissance Philanthropy helps expand funding for data generation.
The release does not state any specific funding or task for the Sanger Institute.
quote_evidence: The groups include the Allen Institute, Broad Institute, Gladstone Institutes, the Human Cell Atlas, the Human Protein Atlas, and the Wellcome Sanger Institute.

Together, the organizations are investing $1.8 billion in funding, data, computation, and new measurement technology, the largest coordinated commitment to generating AI-ready biological data to date.
Google DeepMind, Isomorphic Labs, and Meta are collectively investing $300 million in the Virtual Biology Initiative
why_it_matters_hint: Open, standardised biological data could let researchers train AI models that predict how cells respond to disease and treatment, but the models are a long-term aim.
event_date: 7 Oct 2026 (initiative announced); Sanger angle published by Business Weekly 13 Oct 2026
